correctness.rationale: Exact product density follows from [1, Lemma 2]. For z=exp(i phi), A=(1+i)(2-z)/(1-z), B=(1+i)/(1-z), every interior partial sum is Re(A(1-z^m)) >= alpha=Re(A)-|A| and the terminal sum is Re(A)-Re(B z^k) >= beta=Re(A)-|B|>alpha. Abel summation gives S_k>=alpha a_1+(beta-alpha)a_k>alpha for finite nonnegative delays, including the critical amplitude. Density of irrational rotation powers and a long finite final delay give inf S_k=alpha and actual negative densities for epsilon>1/(1-alpha). Substitution q=cot(phi/2) yields the stated epsilon_star. Source [1] establishes exact normalization and the non-Markovian spectral obstruction for positive epsilon. The extracted standalone checker passed 50,694 independent finite diagnostic assertions; finite sampling is not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The maximum feasible perturbation amplitude is a canonical invariant of a recently introduced explicitly normalized non-Markovian point-process family. The prior paper proves feasibility only for sufficiently small epsilon and provides a conservative value; the result completely characterizes the feasible interval, proves the boundary itself is strictly positive in every finite order, and provides an exact normalized-density infimum. At angle pi/sqrt(2) the admissible amplitude increases from a stated sufficient bound about 0.185 to the exact 0.527. This is a motivated completeness result rather than a random parameter substitution or numerical increment.
